subject: Observability hooks for SDK integration & next steps
messages:
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery call

Thanks for the call today, Marissa — useful conversation. A quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the integration work: 

- Goal: embed LLM-based assistant into our payments help flow. Need low latency for live chat (target p95 < 250ms server-side) and nightly embedding updates for search/rerank.
- Auth: we prefer short-lived service credentials (OIDC) over long-lived API keys for production. Can your SDK support that pattern?
- Routing: want to route sensitive PII traffic to a dedicated/private instance (SLA-backed), and general traffic to a hosted model to save cost. How does routing policy work?
- Structured output / tool calling: we'll need function-calling style responses for executing actions (e.g., create_ticket, fetch_balance). Any best practices?
- Embeddings & reranker: expected embedding latency and recommended vector dims/index? We've been using RedisVector and need ingestion guidance.
- Observability: critical ask — we need trace propagation from our frontend through your inference runtime into downstream ops, and a latency breakdown per hop (network, model_tokenization, model_inference). What headers/log fields do you expose?

Attached: a quick requirements spreadsheet with our constraints.

Next steps for us: confirm auth pattern and observability headers, schedule a technical deep dive with your engineering team.

Thanks,
Alice
Senior Engineering Manager
FinTechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery call

Hi Alice — great speaking with you and Tom. Appreciate the clear requirements doc; we've reviewed it and put together a concise integration plan and observability pattern below. I'll attach a short SDK guide and a mutual action plan (MAP) after this email.

High-level answers and recommendations: 

1) Auth: short-lived service tokens (OIDC) — supported.
   - We recommend using our service-account flow: create a service principal in your IdP, Redwood issues short-lived bearer tokens (JWT) via OIDC. SDKs (Node/Python/Go) include helpers to refresh tokens automatically.
   - For staging access right away we can issue an ephemeral token scoped to your staging project.

2) Routing & policy: fine-grained routing by metadata.
   - Route key options: customer_id, data_class (pii/non-pii), region, priority. Policies can be: prefer(dedicated), prefer(hosted), cost-first (fallback hosted), or latency-first (fallback dedicated).
   - Example: requests with data_class=pii -> route to dedicated pool (SLA), otherwise prefer hosted and fallback to dedicated on high latency.

3) Structured output & function calling: supported via function schemas (JSON Schema) or our typed tool-calling interface.
   - Recommended: declare functions for actions (create_ticket, get_balance) with precise JSON schemas; SDK will validate and populate arguments. We also return a confidence score and execution metadata in the response envelope.

4) Embeddings & reranker: batching + async ingestion.
   - We recommend 1536-d for semantic search on financial FAQ workloads unless you want smaller storage; 768-d is also fine for basic use.
   - Typical single-vector encode latency (hosted) ~ 40-120ms depending on model and batch size; we provide batch endpoints to reduce per-vector latency.
   - Reranker pattern: coarse NN search (top 200) + rerank with lightweight specialized model (zero-shot or supervised) to reorder top-k for final results. We'll share sample reranker glue code.

5) Observability: what we expose and suggested fields.
   - Headers to set/propagate: X-Redwood-Trace (UUID), X-Redwood-Request-Id (short id), X-Client-Request-Id (your correlation id).
   - Response headers we return: X-Redwood-Latency (total_ms), X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown (comma-separated key=ms pairs e.g. network=12,tokenize=8,model_infer=220), X-Redwood-Model (model-name), X-Redwood-Routed-To (pool-id).
   - Logging fields (structured): request_id, trace_id, customer_id, route_policy, model, shard, kv_cache_hits, token_count, input_token_ms, model_infer_ms, total_ms, status_code. These are emitted at INFO for request-level and DEBUG for token-level traces if you enable token_tracing in config.
   - Example log line: {"ts":"...","trace_id":"...","request_id":"...","model":"rwd-llm-13b","route_policy":"latency-first","model_infer_ms":"220","total_ms":"245"}

6) Dashboards & alerts (what we'd provision in your staging workspace):
   - Panels: p50/p95/p99 latency per route/model, token cost per request, embedding ingestion lag, rerank latency, error rate by code, cache hit rate (kv_cache_hits).
   - Alerts: sustained p95 > 300ms, embedding ingestion backlog > 2 hours, increased 4xx/5xx error rate.

Action items / next steps (proposed):
- Redwood: send SDK integration guide + sample header middleware (by EOD 2026-09-08) — owner: Marissa.
- FinTechCo: confirm OIDC service principal details and desired route policy (by 2026-09-10) — owner: Alice.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive for Monday 2026-09-09 10:00 AM PT (30-45m) — owner: Marissa.
- Provide staging credentials and a small sample corpus for embedding ingest (FinTechCo).

I'll attach the SDK doc and MAP now. If this all sounds good we'll kick off the technical deep dive and add Neha/Vivek to the session for architecture and infra details.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@fintechco.com>

Date: 2026-09-08T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability hooks for SDK integration & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications before the deep dive: 

- For X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown, is tokenize included in model_infer or separate? We need token-level breakdown for troubleshooting generation delays.
- For embeddings: is 1536-d available across your hosted/dedicated variants or only on specific families? Anywhere we can see perf benchmarks?
- For auth: curious if you support automatic rotation of staging tokens via Vault/Key Manager integrations (we use HashiCorp Vault).

We'll confirm the OIDC details and will accept the Monday slot — Tom and I will be on the call. Can you add Neha and Vivek invite links? Also, attaching a short note: what SLA credits look like for p95 misses — Tom will follow up with procurement later.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alice

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability hooks for SDK integration & next steps

Perfect — confirmed for Monday 2026-09-09 10:00 AM PT. Calendar invite sent (video link + dial-in). Tom/Alice, we'll bring a short runbook and a sample dashboard. 

Quick answers inline: 
- tokenize is reported separately in X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown (tokenize=ms) so you can isolate tokenization vs model_infer. We can also enable token_tracing on staging if you want to capture token-level timings for a short window.
- 1536-d is available on our recommended semantic models on both hosted and Dedicated variants; perf varies by model and hardware (we'll include a perf matrix in the doc).
- Vault rotation: yes — we have integrations with HashiCorp Vault and can rotate staging secrets automatically; production OIDC integration works well with short-lived tokens (we'll share an example Terraform snippet).

Attachments included in this thread:
- redwood_sdk_integration_guide.pdf (SDK snippets: Node/Python auth helpers, header middleware, example function-call schemas, embedding batch ingestion)
- FT-4832_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (milestones, owners, dates)

Sample header + log field snippet (for quick copy/paste):

Request header example:
X-Client-Request-Id: fintechco-req-12345
X-Redwood-Trace: 4f8a6e2b-9d3a-4c8f-b7f1-2a5d6e9b0c11
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...

Response headers example:
X-Redwood-Request-Id: rwd-req-8b9d
X-Redwood-Latency: 245
X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: network=12,tokenize=8,model_infer=220,post_process=5
X-Redwood-Model: rwd-llm-13b-512q
X-Redwood-Routed-To: pool-dedicated-us-west-2-3

Suggested log fields (JSON):
["ts","trace_id","request_id","client_request_id","customer_id","route_policy","model","kv_cache_hits","input_token_ms","model_infer_ms","total_ms","status_code"]

See you Monday — we'll bring the engineers and a copy of the perf matrix.

Best,
Marissa
